result.summary: The intersection features marked continental crosswalks and continuous sidewalks within a commercial context. However, the environment lacks visible pedestrian-specific signal heads at a signalized intersection, and utility poles are positioned close to the curb ramps, potentially impacting accessibility and sightlines.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: The intersection is controlled by vehicle traffic lights, but there are no visible pedestrian signal heads to indicate safe crossing intervals.
hazards.location_in_image: At all corners of the intersection

hazards.name: Utility Pole Placement
hazards.description: Large utility poles are located immediately adjacent to the curb ramps, which may restrict the effective width of the pedestrian path or create minor sightline obstructions.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground corner near the fire hydrant

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to all legs of the intersection to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and increase the visibility of pedestrians waiting to cross.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Implement a signal timing change that gives pedestrians a head start before parallel vehicle traffic receives a green light.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with high-visibility continental crosswalks and overhead traffic signals within a residential context. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the large trees at the corners may create visual obstructions between drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Large trees and dense vegetation at the intersection corners may obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching or turning motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Corners of the intersection, particularly the near left and far left quadrants.

hazards.name: Pavement Degradation
hazards.description: Visible cracking and wear in the asphalt surface within the intersection area.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and center of the roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Constructing curb extensions would reduce the crossing distance for pedestrians and improve their visibility to drivers by moving the waiting area past the line of trees.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management (Daylighting)
interventions.description: Trimming low-hanging branches and thinning vegetation near the corners to ensure clear sightlines between all road users.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Programming the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light, reducing conflicts with turning traffic.

result.summary: The intersection features marked continental crosswalks and sidewalks but lacks dedicated pedestrian signals. Significant visual obstructions from dense vegetation on the corner may hinder visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sight line obstruction
hazards.description: Dense vegetation on the corner blocks the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image at the corner of the intersection

hazards.name: Missing pedestrian signals
hazards.description: The intersection is signalized for vehicles but lacks visible pedestrian-specific signals to indicate safe crossing times.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim or remove the dense bushes at the corner to improve sight lines for all road users.

result.summary: The intersection features standard pedestrian infrastructure including marked ladder-style crosswalks, curb ramps, and dedicated pedestrian signals. The environment is primarily residential with mature trees and well-maintained sidewalks, though it lacks physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions.

hazards.name: Utility Pole Obstruction
hazards.description: A large utility pole is positioned near the curb ramp, which may slightly narrow the clear path for pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground corner at the intersection

interventions.description: Constructing bulb-outs would shorten the crossing distance and increase the visibility of pedestrians to approaching motorists.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Implement a signal timing change to allow pedestrians to enter the crosswalk before vehicles receive a green light, reducing conflicts with turning traffic.
